I have farmed this land a long time, so I would not make big changes this year. On 25.1 mu with a wheat-maize rotation and only two people in the household, I would keep the whole area in the same rotation because it is familiar, matches my well irrigation, and gives me the most stable grain output. For wheat, I would use an improved variety rather than old saved seed because I want steady emergence, better disease resistance, and a reliable yield. I would put fertilizer on at a moderate level, not too high, because I care more about a safe harvest than chasing the absolute top yield. Since I have well irrigation, I would plan two irrigations for wheat, mainly at the key water-demand stages, because wheat in Hebei usually needs water support for stable production. I would use rotary tillage because it is practical for me, fits my usual machinery habits, and prepares a workable seedbed without too much trouble. I would also spray a couple of times if needed to control weeds and disease and protect yield.

For maize, I would plant a hybrid because maize hybrids usually give me stronger yield and better stand uniformity. I would keep fertilizer slightly higher on nitrogen than wheat because maize responds strongly to it, but I would still stay in a moderate range to control cost and avoid waste. I would irrigate about two times if rainfall is not enough, because summer maize can still suffer if key stages are dry even with the monsoon season. I would also keep pesticide use to a limited number of applications, mainly for weeds and major insects, because I want clean field management but I do not want unnecessary spraying. I would continue with rotary tillage here too, because with my experience and labor situation, I prefer a simple and stable system that I know I can finish on time. My goal this year would be dependable yields from both crops, not risky changes.
